title: Catalase–peroxidase as the INH-activating enzyme node
dek: Wikipedia catalase page plus KatG identity. Alleles and INH doses stay on tb-katg-inha / tb-isoniazid.
story: Catalase on Wikipedia is a peroxide-dismantling enzyme. Mtb's KatG is a catalase–peroxidase that also activates isoniazid — a dual-use protein that textbooks love and DST lives on.
Simplfy already walks S315T and inhA promoter on dedicated plates. This card is the encyclopedia enzyme name so a catalase search does not invent a new INH monograph.
Loss of catalase activity is a lab phenotype that sometimes accompanies katG loss-of-function. It is not a WHO dose.
deep: INH–NAD adduct against InhA is the target story (tb-isoniazid, tb-mycolates).
KatG S315T is a common compromise allele: enough catalase to live, less INH activation.
ETH/InhA is a different activation path (EthA) — do not merge because both mention InhA.

visual.caption: Prodrug in, KatG activation, InhA block. Wikipedia names catalase; clinic plates name the alleles.
